about: A Honduran-made Punch from General Cigar with a reddish Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper. It was sold as a seasonal limited release from 2001 until it became a year-round line in January 2025.
notes: Despite the name, the wrapper is Ecuadorian Sumatra, not Corojo. Holt's rates it medium-full, Neptune rates it full. It was a limited seasonal release until 2025.
verifyNotes: Added the En Crystale (5 1/2 x 54), which Punch and halfwheel both list. Everything else matched Punch, halfwheel, Holt's and Neptune. Punch's own size chart rounds El Doble to 6 x 60; halfwheel, Holt's and Neptune give 5 7/8 x 60, so that was kept.

about: An all-Honduran Punch from General Cigar, introduced in 2003. It uses a sun-grown Havana-seed wrapper over Honduran binder and filler.
notes: Holt's and Famous rate it medium-full, Neptune rates it medium. Famous lists the Sesenta as 6 x 60. A separate Gran Puro Nicaragua line with a Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper was added in 2017.

about: The core Honduran Punch line from General Cigar, now sold under the Clásico name. It pairs an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper with a Connecticut Broadleaf binder and a three-country filler.
notes: Clásico is the current name for the original Honduran Punch, which dates to 1969. Holt's and Neptune rate it medium, Famous says medium to full. A Clásico Maduro with a Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper is sold alongside it.

Punch's chart gives Grandote as 6 1/4 x 60; Neptune and Famous give 5 7/8 x 60, which was kept. 1969 is Neptune's date for the Honduran Punch. factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua
about: Billed by General Cigar as the strongest Punch, made for it by AJ Fernandez in Estelí, Nicaragua. It was the first General-owned Punch made outside the company's Honduran factory.
notes: Famous and Neptune list the Brute as 6 x 60; halfwheel and Holt's list 6 1/4 x 60.

about: A value-priced Punch from General Cigar, launched in 2020 as an everyday smoke. The original blend uses Nicaraguan Habano wrapper and binder over Nicaraguan and Honduran filler.
notes: This is the original Habano blend. Knuckle Buster Maduro (2022, Connecticut Broadleaf) and Shade (Ecuadorian Connecticut) are separate blends. Famous calls the Habano medium to full; Punch and Neptune say medium.

about: A fuller Punch introduced in 2015 as a tribute to the original non-Cuban Punch blend. It uses an Ecuadorian Corojo wrapper grown for the line over a Connecticut Habano binder.
notes: Famous lists the binder as Nicaraguan; Punch and halfwheel say Connecticut Habano. Punch and retailers call it full, though the brand manager described it as medium-plus in 2021.

about: A Honduran-made Punch that General Cigar produced as an exclusive for the retailer Cigars International. It has an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper over Nicaraguan and Honduran filler.

about: A Honduran-made Punch from General Cigar sold in a few traditional sizes, mainly the 7 1/4 x 54 Chateau L. The natural version uses an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper.

about: Released in 2014 to mark Manuel "Manolo" Quesada Jr.'s 40 years in the cigar business. The regular sizes use a Mexican San Andrés wrapper over Dominican binder and Dominican and Nicaraguan filler.
notes: The Corona Clasica size is a different blend with an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper, known as the Manolo blend. Toro Press and Salomon Press were limited editions. Full is Neptune's rating; halfwheel's review of the 4 x 50 size found it medium.

about: Introduced in 2015 as what was then Quesada's most premium line, built around Dominican San Vicente tobacco from the 1997 harvest. The cigars are aged for at least a year after rolling.
notes: Production is limited by the supply of 1997 vintage tobacco. Oscuro (Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper) and Barber Pole versions are separate releases. Strength is Famous Smoke's rating. Famous lists the Robusto as 4 3/4 x 52; halfwheel says 4 1/2 x 52.

about: An annual limited release from Quesada, first made in 2011 and blended to pair with the Märzen-style beer served at Oktoberfest. It ships each year in late summer.

about: A Quesada line launched in January 2013 with the tagline "Embrace Uncertainty". Quesada deliberately keeps the blend secret so smokers judge it without preconceptions.

about: The first blend in Noel Rojas's Street Tacos series, released in March 2021. It uses an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler from the Somoto region.
